execution_context.file_location: malicious Google Play app (disguised as Web3 tool)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Code that abuses the WalletConnect protocol to steal private keys or sign unauthorized transactions, exfiltrating cryptocurrency to attacker-controlled wallets.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code interacts with the WalletConnect protocol to prompt users for wallet access, then exfiltrates private keys or signs unauthorized transactions, resulting in theft of cryptocurrency.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app masquerades as a legitimate Web3 tool but performs unauthorized access and exfiltration of sensitive wallet data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate Web3 tool should never exfiltrate private keys or sign transactions without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may use WalletConnect to facilitate user-approved transactions, but never to steal funds.
key_indicators: Abuse of WalletConnect protocol for unauthorized access
Exfiltration of private keys or transaction signing without user consent
Disguised as a legitimate app to evade detection

execution_context.file_location: ChatGPT macOS app memory (via indirect prompt injection)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Injected code via prompt injection that persists in app memory, intercepts user inputs, and exfiltrates chat data to an external server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the injected code remains resident in memory, intercepts all user inputs and future chat sessions, and exfiltrates this data to an attacker-controlled server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code achieves persistence in memory and continuously exfiltrates sensitive user data, which is not expected in a legitimate chat application.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate chat apps should not allow prompt injection to result in persistent spyware or data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Debugging or telemetry code may collect usage data, but not persistently exfiltrate all user inputs.
key_indicators: Persistence in app memory via prompt injection
Continuous interception and exfiltration of user data

execution_context.file_location: DLL loaded by legitimate application (DLL Hijacking)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious DLL with exported functions matching those expected by the legitimate application, containing payload code for persistence, privilege escalation, or data exfiltration.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the legitimate application loads the malicious DLL, the exported functions execute attacker-controlled code, enabling persistence, privilege escalation, or data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLL hijacking is a well-known technique for executing malicious code in the context of trusted applications.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate DLLs should not contain code for persistence, privilege escalation, or data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom DLLs may be used for legitimate plugin systems, but not for malicious payloads.
key_indicators: DLL placed in application search path
Exports matching legitimate DLLs but containing malicious payloads
Execution in context of trusted application

execution_context.file_location: KLogEXE and FPSpy malware samples (Windows executables)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Keylogger code that captures keystrokes and exfiltrates them; backdoor code that collects data and executes attacker commands.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware captures user keystrokes and system data, then exfiltrates this information to attacker infrastructure. The backdoor also allows remote command execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Keylogging and remote command execution are classic malicious behaviors not found in legitimate software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not capture keystrokes or allow remote command execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools may have similar features, but with user consent and transparency.

attack_chain.action: User installs malicious app (e.g., crypto drainer, ChatGPT macOS app, or DLL placed for hijacking).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is executed in the context of a trusted application or environment.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes at runtime, abusing permissions to access sensitive data (wallets, keystrokes, chat data, etc.).
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is collected or attacker gains control.

attack_chain.action: Collected data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure, or attacker executes further commands (e.g., privilege escalation, ransomware deployment).
attack_chain.leads_to: Data theft, financial loss, or further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests from apps claiming to be wallet tools or chat clients
Persistence of injected code in application memory (prompt injection)
DLLs loaded from non-standard locations with unexpected exports
Keylogging or remote command execution in non-administrative tools
file_indicators: Unknown or unsigned DLLs in application directories
Android apps requesting excessive permissions for wallet access
Unusual executable files (e.g., KLogEXE, FPSpy) present on system
network_indicators: Connections to known crypto drainer or APT infrastructure
Exfiltration to attacker-controlled domains or IPs
Unexpected outbound traffic from chat or wallet apps
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for applications that request or access sensitive data (wallets, keystrokes, chat logs) and initiate outbound connections to untrusted domains. Detect prompt injection or memory-resident code in chat applications. Watch for DLLs loaded from non-standard paths and for executables with keylogging or backdoor capabilities. Use behavioral analysis to flag apps that exfiltrate data or perform unauthorized actions.
